name: Bryce Canyon National Park
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Bryce Canyon National Park in southwestern Utah is renowned for its extraordinary collection of hoodoos — tall, thin spires of rock formed by frost weathering and stream erosion of the Claron Formation limestone. Despite its name, Bryce Canyon is not a true canyon but rather a series of natural amphitheaters carved into the eastern edge of the Paunsaugunt Plateau. The area was designated a national monument in 1923 and became a national park in 1928. The Paiute people, who inhabited the region for centuries before European contact, called the hoodoos "red rocks standing like men in a bowl-shaped canyon" in their oral tradition.
